title: coordkit cross-machine dispatch payload
description: Payload of the dispatch.* event family (`cobus dispatch`, scripts/core/scripts/dispatch.sh). It rides in the event envelope's `body` as a compact JSON string (covered by the eid) and is mirrored as the envelope's top-level `dispatch` object. The envelope `subject` is the dispatch id. Dispatch state is a PROJECTION: replay one id's events in (clock.p, create-first, eid) order — open → accepted → done | released | expired; released/expired reopen the dispatch for another accept (new epoch); the first `dispatch.accepted` per epoch wins. Events carry no `seq`. See docs/DISPATCH.md.

ts.description: Epoch seconds when this event was written (lease math uses this; ordering uses the envelope clock.p).

task.description: Ledger task subject (slug) this dispatch hands over. Present on `dispatch` and `dispatch.accepted`.

title.description: `dispatch` only: the task's human title (exported to a worker child as COORDKIT_TASK_TITLE).

target.description: `dispatch` only: who may accept. Empty object = anyone. All present constraints must hold.

needs.description: Capability requirements: every key must be present and truthy in the acceptor's caps; a string value must equal the acceptor's value ("*", "" or true mean 'present').

lease_s.description: `dispatch` only: lease length in seconds granted on accept/renew (default 1800).

priority.description: `dispatch` only: lower is picked first by `accept --auto` (default 5).

note.description: `dispatch` only: free text for the acceptor.

by.description: accepted/renewed/released/done: the machine+actor performing the transition.

holder.description: `dispatch.expired` only: whose lapsed lease was reaped.

lease_until.description: accepted/renewed/expired: epoch seconds the lease is (was) valid until. Also mirrored in the envelope `lease.until`.

epoch.description: `dispatch.accepted` only: the open epoch being accepted (1 on first open, +1 after each release/expiry). An accept whose epoch does not match the current epoch on read is ignored.
